decisions_made: Followed the continuation handoff's NEXT TARGET and smaller-first ordering exactly, processing all 9 remaining count-1-tier files in the listed order without deviation.

For the three large axiom-schema inductive files (Temporal/ProofSystem/Axioms.lean, ConservativeExtension/ExtDerivation.lean, Bimodal/ProofSystem/Axioms.lean), identified a new dominant style.emptyLine sub-pattern not seen in prior cycles: blank lines used as visual separators between constructors and around '-- Layer N' comments, all inside one giant `inductive ... where` command. Fixed by locating the command's exact span via a declaration-keyword grep, then mechanically deleting every blank line strictly inside that span (verified via diff that only blank lines were ever removed, before rebuilding) while leaving the between-command separator blank line untouched. Recorded as new category C8.

For Decidability/ProofExtraction.lean's longLine sites, used two techniques: mechanical continuation-line wrapping for def signatures and a multi-line let-chain (splitting a type annotation across indented lines, keeping ':=' attached per the P5 hazard), and -- for one long diagnostic string literal that could not be wrapped by splitting an expression -- a Lean string-gap continuation (backslash immediately before a newline inside a string literal, whose leading whitespace on the next line is elided). Verified the string-gap approach compiles clean and preserves the exact original wording via git diff, rather than shortening the message (which would have been a safer but content-altering fallback).

For Decidability/Closure.lean's unusedSectionVars warnings, used the declaration-scoped `omit [Hashable Atom] in` idiom per the existing P2/category guidance for this specific linter category (distinct from the omit-breaks-compilation case documented for unusedDecidableInType) -- verified safe by a clean rebuild.

For the two heavily-imported core files (Separation/Defs.lean with 10 direct importers, Decidability/Tableau.lean with importers that themselves aggregate the whole Decidability/ subtree), used the plan's explicit exemption for heavily-imported core files: verified via a full rebuild of the aggregating module (Metalogic/Separation.lean, 811 jobs; Decidability.lean, 809 jobs) rather than enumerating and rebuilding each direct importer individually.

Re-baselined check-lint-suppressions.sh once at cycle end via --update after confirming the live count (25) matched the expected repo-wide total (14 upstream + 5 permanent exceptions + 6 in the deferred Interface.lean = 25), rather than after every individual file -- all 9 individual per-file commits landed first with the ratchet still at the stale 34 ceiling (which permits decreases), then a single --update commit closed the cycle.

Ran the full CSLib CI pipeline (all 8 steps except the cache fetch, already warm) once at cycle end, matching cycle 25's granularity choice -- per-file scoped rebuilds plus downstream-importer (or aggregating-module) rebuilds already provided per-commit verification.

Fully rewrote the plan's RESUME HERE section, added a 'Done (cycle 26)' backfill table with per-file results and commit hashes, added new category C8 to Accumulated findings, and updated the plan header, Phase 5 heading stats, baseline table, and Definition-of-Done row -- all in a single dedicated plan-update commit (b6e00409), matching prior-cycle practice.

Did not attempt Interface.lean (3048 lines, count-6 tier, deliberately deferred -- explicitly flagged in the continuation note as needing a dedicated large-context-budget cycle) or re-investigate either of Phase 7's closed blockers, matching this task's standing scope constraints. Stopped cleanly after closing the count-1 tier rather than opportunistically starting the count-6 file with reduced remaining context.
